evals.name: rewrite-cli-readme
evals.prompt: Copy the project in ../../eval-fixtures/readme-generator/logtail-cli to a scratch directory and rewrite its README there so a new user can install it and run it within a minute. The copy has no git remote, so skip the repo sync.
evals.expected_output: Fixture logtail-cli. Rewrite mode: README.backup.md holds the original. README.md opens with # logtail, a one-sentence pitch, ## Install (Node.js 18 prerequisite, then npm install -g logtail-cli in its own block), and ## Quick start (a logtail command taken from the original README, then its result). The options table, the ~/.logtailrc configuration, the development commands and the MIT license all come after the landing section. The options table includes --since from src/cli.js. The run closes with a Final Report.
expectations: Created README.backup.md before writing README.md, and recorded sync: skipped with its reason
README.md starts with the H1 `# logtail`, then a pitch of one sentence of 25 words or fewer, before any `##` heading
Outside <details>, the first fenced code block is `npm install -g logtail-cli`, under an Install heading that states the Node.js 18 requirement
The second fenced code block is a logtail command taken from the original README (for example `my-server | logtail --level warn`), under a Quick start heading
No mermaid block, table, or other `##` heading appears before the Quick start command's output or result sentence
The Quick start result is either output copied from a source or one sentence describing the result, and the run labels it as not run (no invented output block)
The original Options, Configuration (~/.logtailrc), Development and License content is all present after the landing section, and the run lists where each original section went
The options table includes --since, with its description taken from src/cli.js
Printed a Step Completion Report after each step, ending with a Self-review report of 8 checks

The Final Report opens with `Result:` and a status matching the checks, cites the install and Quick start sources as path:line on `Evidence:`, labels assumptions on `Uncertainty:`, and its `Decision:` line names the pending choice or says No approval needed

evals.name: create-library-readme
evals.prompt: Copy the project in ../../eval-fixtures/readme-generator/slugkit to a scratch directory and write a README for it there. It has no git remote, so skip the repo sync.
evals.expected_output: Fixture slugkit (no README). Create mode: no backup. README.md opens with # slugkit, a one-sentence pitch, ## Install (Python 3.9+ prerequisite from pyproject.toml, then pip install slugkit, because .github/workflows/release.yml publishes to PyPI), and ## Quick start (from slugkit import slugify; slugify("Hello, World!") with the result hello-world taken from tests/test_slugify.py). Usage covers separator and max_length; License names MIT. No CLI command is invented. The run closes with a Final Report.
expectations: Picked Create mode and wrote README.md; no file other than README.md was created or changed
The first fenced code block is `pip install slugkit`, and the run cites .github/workflows/release.yml (the PyPI publish step) or pyproject.toml as its source
The Install section states the Python 3.9 or later requirement from pyproject.toml
The Quick start code imports slugify from slugkit and calls it on an input from tests/test_slugify.py, and shows the matching output from that test (for example hello-world)
Nothing but the H1, the pitch and the two landing headings appears before the Quick start output
The Usage section covers the separator and max_length parameters, taken from src/slugkit/__init__.py, and invents no other parameter or CLI command
A License section names MIT
Printed a Step Completion Report after each step

The Final Report opens with `Result:` and a status matching the checks, its `Evidence:` line names the sources of the install command and the Quick start, and its `Decision:` line names the pending choice or says No approval needed

evals.name: landing-only-fix
evals.prompt: Copy the project in ../../eval-fixtures/readme-generator/logtail-cli to a scratch directory. The rest of its README is fine, so only fix the top there: install and a quick example should come first. No git remote, so skip the sync.
evals.expected_output: Landing only mode: README.backup.md holds the original. Only the old opening (the title, the intro line and the Installation section) changes: H1, pitch, Install with npm install -g logtail-cli, and Quick start with a logtail command from the README. Every section after the old opening (Usage with its Options table, Configuration, Development, License) matches the backup byte for byte. The run closes with a Final Report.
expectations: Picked Landing only mode and created README.backup.md before writing

The new opening has the H1, a one-sentence pitch, an Install heading with `npm install -g logtail-cli` in a fenced block, and a Quick start heading with a logtail command from the original README in a fenced block
The Usage, Configuration, Development and License sections are byte-identical to README.backup.md
Did not add an options table entry, a diagram, or any new section below the opening

The Final Report opens with `Result:` and a status matching the checks, its `Evidence:` line reports the byte-for-byte check of the later sections, and its `Decision:` line names the pending choice or says No approval needed

evals.name: sell-the-project
evals.prompt: make my README sell the project — I want more GitHub stars and contributors
evals.expected_output: Rewrite mode with a benefit-led pitch and features, but the landing section stays first: pitch, Install, Quick start. A Contributing section appears in the detail area. No fabricated stars, downloads or testimonials. README.backup.md created. The run closes with a Final Report.
expectations: Created README.backup.md before rewriting README.md
The pitch is one benefit-led sentence that passes the copy test (visualizable, falsifiable, specific to this project), placed under the project-name H1
Install and Quick start still come before any features, diagram, or social proof
A Contributing or Development section in the detail area tells contributors how to set up and run the tests, from the project's files
Used real numbers or [placeholder] markers; no fabricated stars, downloads, users or testimonials
The Final Report opens with `Result:` and a status matching the checks, and its `Evidence:` line cites only checks that ran

evals.name: framework-keeps-landing-order
evals.prompt: rewrite my README as a landing page, use the StoryBrand framework
evals.expected_output: Rewrite mode. StoryBrand shapes the pitch and the first detail section (the user as hero, the project as guide), and the run says so. The landing order does not change: pitch, Install, Quick start come first. README.backup.md created. The run closes with a Final Report.
expectations: Told the user that StoryBrand applies to the pitch and the first detail section, and that the opening order stays pitch, Install, Quick start
The README still opens with the H1, the pitch, Install and Quick start, in that order, before any StoryBrand section
The first detail section frames the reader as the hero and the project as the guide
Created README.backup.md before rewriting
Did not build an HTML page or write any file other than README.md and its backup
The Final Report opens with `Result:` and a status matching the checks

evals.name: github-action-merged-snippet
evals.prompt: Write the README for my GitHub Action in this repo. action.yml is at the root, and the existing README only has a title.
evals.expected_output: Rewrite mode: the title-only README is backed up to README.backup.md. The landing section merges Install and Quick start into one workflow snippet under ## Quick start, with the action's inputs taken from action.yml; there is no separate ## Install. An inputs table from action.yml follows in the detail area. The run closes with a Final Report.
expectations: Picked Rewrite mode and created README.backup.md before writing, because a README already exists
The opening has no `## Install` heading; one workflow YAML snippet under a Quick start heading shows a `uses:` line for the action
Every input in the snippet and in the inputs table comes from action.yml; none is invented
No diagram, table or other heading appears before the snippet
The Final Report opens with `Result:` and a status matching the checks, and cites action.yml as the source of the snippet
